Epoxides are three-membered cyclic ethers that are highly strained and reactive. Mercaptans (thiols) and other organic sulfides contain sulfur atoms with nucleophilic properties.

When epoxides react with mercaptans:
1. The reaction typically involves nucleophilic ring-opening of the epoxide
2. This is often an exothermic reaction
3. Thiols are excellent nucleophiles and can react vigorously with epoxides
4. This reaction is commonly used in polymer chemistry

The most significant hazard when epoxides react with mercaptans is likely violent polymerization. The nucleophilic attack of the mercaptan on the epoxide ring can initiate a chain reaction, especially in the presence of basic catalysts or at elevated temperatures. This polymerization can be exothermic and potentially violent if not controlled.
